properties.name: Two more unreachable declared properties, and the reason nobody caught them: the reach instrument only looks at properties NOTHING has ever written, so a schema default hides one
properties.statement:
REPORTED 2026-09-07 by the dev_storyflow agent (peer feedback lines 7286-7303), as friction rather than as a bug: "add_epoch lost `description` (it had one before?) - the ordering and the must-nots had to go into the name, which is now a paragraph. add_requirement lost `priority`. Both fine, both cost a round-trip."

TIER 1 FIRST (rule:every-failure-is-searched-and-every-cause-is-root-caused-before-it-is-written): searched the design before reading any code. This is a RECURRENCE of a named class, not a new finding - req:declared-vocabulary-is-reachable-from-the-surface exists, fact:note-was-instances-five-and-six-of-unreachable-declared-vocabulary counted instances five and six, and fact:defect-add-verification-cannot-reach-its-own-fields is the same shape on another constructor. These are instances SEVEN and EIGHT.

THE REPORTER'S PREMISE IS WRONG AND THAT MATTERS. Nothing was lost. `git log -S` over service.rs shows AddEpochReq has never in its history carried `description`, and no request struct has ever carried `priority`. The fields were declared in the schema and never offered by a typed tool, which is a different defect from a regression and has a different fix. Their own wish #37 - say whether a rejected field MOVED or was REMOVED - is exactly the missing sentence that would have told them so, and is recorded separately as an idea.

MEASURED, 2026-09-07, against the v0.51.0 export and toolsnaps:
- `DesignEpoch.description` is declared (schema/temporal.yaml:20, fulltext) and is the type's EMBEDDING FIELD (temporal.yaml:23). 8 of 202 epochs carry one, all written through create_node. add_epoch offers id, name, epoch_type, sequence - four params, per tools/toolsnaps/add_epoch.json. So the field search embeds an epoch by cannot be written by the tool that makes one.
- `Requirement.priority` is declared with `default: medium` (schema/core.yaml:50). 207 requirements: 193 sit at the injected default, 14 carry something else, all written through create_node. The string "priority" appears in NO toolsnap - not one of 169 tools accepts it anywhere on the surface.

THE CAUSE, and it is the instrument rather than either constructor. tools/vocabulary_reach.py reports a property only when THE TYPE IS USED, THE PROPERTY IS NEVER USED, AND NO TYPED TOOL ACCEPTS THE NAME. The middle clause is what fails here. Requirement.priority reads as used on every single requirement because dynograph INJECTS the schema default at write (fact:defaults-are-injected-by-dynograph-at-write), so a property no tool can set looks fully adopted. DesignEpoch.description reads as used because eight generic create_node calls wrote one. Both are therefore filtered out before the reachability question is ever asked, and the instrument reported 14 candidates today with neither of these among them. A user found in one session what the instrument was built to find and structurally cannot.

WHY THE FILTER EXISTS is not in dispute - it was there to keep the list actionable, since an unreachable property that everyone writes anyway through the generic path is a weaker finding than one nobody can write at all. The defect is that the two questions were fused: REACHABILITY (does any typed tool accept this name?) is a property of the surface and needs no usage data, and ADOPTION (does anyone write it?) is a property of the graph. Answering them in one filter makes each unable to report what the other hides.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: how many further instances the unfused instrument would report. That measurement has not been taken - it needs the reachability pass run without the usage filter, which is the fix rather than a diagnostic. Nor does it establish that either field SHOULD be added to its constructor; that is a judgement about whether the property is worth writing, and the reporter wanted both.
